correctness.rationale: The graphical arrangement deletes exactly the comparison for 1 and 2. A chamber merges exactly the two adjacent orderings of those labels unless other comparisons already force their order. For an interior adjacent pair with preceding set S, the prefix basis exhibits the core generators e1,e2,e3,e1-e2+e3 in basis coordinates, with all other generators an independent orthant. At either end of the order the vanishing extreme prefix gives one redundant generator and the surviving basis is related by an integral elementary column operation. In the interior the four rays are extreme, the defining relation is primitive, and each proper core face is generated by part of an integral basis. In the dual, x,y,z are nonnegative with y<=x+z; assigning the y units to x or z gives the four semigroup generators, and exchanging one assignment for the other gives the sole binomial uv-wz. Its singular support is the origin in every characteristic, as the four partial derivatives vanish exactly there; the lowest-degree form is quadratic so the transverse multiplicity is two. Each maximal cone contains at most one singular core. All cones containing a given core use the same ordered blocks S,(1,2),T; equality of the cores would force the same set S, since differences of core prefix pairs span the two label directions and the two other blocks are separately identified by nonempty proper prefixes before and after the pair. Equivalently, the interior of the core has coordinates constant on S and on T, with both coordinates 1 and 2 strictly between those two levels. Thus the corresponding orbit closures are disjoint. The saturated span is generated by u_S and the two individual coordinate classes for labels 1 and 2. Quotienting kills those two classes and the all-ones vectors of both S and T; the remaining chain rays give exactly the two braid fans in their own lattices. Dimensions give codimension three. The only nonunimodular cones are nonsimplicial, giving equality with the non-Q-factorial support. The singular fixed-point count is the sum of |S|!|T|! over nonempty proper S, giving (n-3)(n-2)!; merging the adjacent permutations subtracts (n-1)! from n!, and subtraction gives the smooth count. This works in the boundary dimension n=4 as well as all higher n.
residual_risks: The check concerns reduced support and transverse charts, not a global singular subscheme. The supplied finite checker is supplementary to the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The general graphical-fan description, simplicity test, and toric smoothness criteria are known. In the strongest comparisons the distinct result is the all-n disjoint decomposition as an integral product-star family, with uniform conifold slices and the matching census. A closely related same-day record finds conifold strata plus different isolated singularities for a graph with two edges removed; its theorem does not specialize to this one-edge family.

value.rationale: One missing edge is the minimal perturbation of the smooth permutohedral case. The finding explains how exponentially many singular components can remain disjoint, identifies each component's toric type and transverse singularity, and makes the whole family explicit in every dimension. The useful content is the complete geometry, not just a small exact count or a simplicity diagnostic.
residual_risks: Value is for this particular normal-fan family; extension to more edge deletions or other realizations is not established.
